newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA BLAMES BOLIVIA FOR MATCH BRAWL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA BLAMES BOLIVIA FOR MATCH BRAWL.

text.p: Argentina's Soccer Association (AFA) has written to world soccer body FIFA to complain about the organisation of last week's violent World Cup clash with Bolivia.
The game in La Paz deteriorated twice into brawls and ended with a 2-1 defeat for Argentina.

"This Association wants to stress that it considers the organisation of the match between Argentina and Bolivia to have been deficient, starting with the lamentable and extremely repressive behaviour of the security personnel," the AFA wrote, according to state news agency Telam.

But the AFA added that a gash to the face of Argentina's Julio Cruz, which was widely shown in Argentine media, was the result of an accident and not caused by being punched by a Bolivian team assistant.
The wild attack on Cruz was one of the boxing highlights of a match which also included Argentine goalkeeper Ignacio Gonzalez knocking a Bolivian to the ground by headbutting him from behind.

The Argentine press mainly accused the Bolivians of starting the fights but admitted their national team played poorly. The fixture was touted as a grudge match from the start, after comments by Argentine coach Daniel Passarella that being forced to play in La Paz at 14,000 feet (3,600) above sea level was "inhuman".
